findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!”, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in the logo blue. On this page that blue marks only things you can act on: the Get in touch button, the underlined related-article link and Play again. Plain quoted text in the same blue looks like a link, which breaks the house rule that a colour marking links never colours non-link text. The italic and the larger size already make the quote stand out without the blue.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page, who sees blue words and tries to click them, or who can no longer trust blue to mean a link. Angélique, who will copy this treatment for quotes in every new post, so the clash will spread across the blog.

findings.where: Nav bar, the logo lockup at desktop
findings.fault: The firm's name, MMM INFRA, is set smaller than its descriptor beside it, MOSELEY INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISORY SERVICES. The descriptor is also stacked in three lines, so the subtitle outranks the name and the name reads as a caption under the arches.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo makes MMM INFRA the wordmark with the descriptor beside it as a secondary line. A first-time visitor, who takes the long descriptor to be the firm's name.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the line “precise, light, quick”; article specimen, the related-article title “Streamlining the PPP Process…”
findings.fault: The tile states its own rule that Source Sans is for the nav, buttons, labels and dates only. It then sets a display line, the motion sketch's heading, and an article title in semibold Source Sans. Elsewhere every heading and article title is in Gelasio, so like text is set two ways.
findings.who_objects: The designers of the layout round and the animation round, who take the type pair from this tile and get one stated rule but two practices. Mark, judging whether the site speaks in one Georgia-like voice.
